rule_or_fact: A Member State sells CBAM certificates on a common central platform to authorised declarants established in that Member State.
legal_basis_or_document: Reg. (EU) 2023/956 Art. 20(1), as amended by Reg. (EU) 2025/2083 Art. 1(16)(a)

rule_or_fact: 30 September 2027 for the 2026 declaration year; certificates bought in 2027 for 2026 may only be repurchased in 2027; unsurrendered 2026-year certificates are cancelled on 1 Nov 2027.
Weekly average of EU ETS auction closing prices (Art. 21(1)); for the 2026 declaration year the price is the quarterly average of the quarter of importation (new Art. 21(1a)).

To the selling Member State: the Regulation makes Member States responsible for 'correctly establishing and collecting revenues' (recital 64); there is no article assigning certificate revenue to the Union budget or earmarking its use.
legal_basis_or_document: Reg. (EU) 2023/956 recital 64, Art. 20(1); no revenue-use article found by full-text search

rule_or_fact: Not an EU own resource. Recital 74 only says the Union is working towards a new own resource based on CBAM certificate sales.
Fees paid by declarants for the central platform are Union internal assigned revenue (first procurement contract), not Member State revenue; any remainder goes to the Union budget.
Uniform call rate of 75% of revenues from the sale of CBAM certificates to the EU budget; Commission estimate EUR 1.4 bn a year on average in the next MFF (EUR 1.5 bn in current prices, per the ECA).
legal_basis_or_document: COM(2025) 574 final of 16 Jul 2025 (Art. 3(1)(h), recital 15, application from [1 January 2028]); ECA Opinion 04/2026 para 22-23

rule_or_fact: Negotiating Box of 10 Oct 2026 keeps CBAM as new own resource with the call rate in square brackets at [90]% (not agreed); Presidency note of 4 Sep 2026: CBAM is the most consensual of the five proposed new own resources, many Member States open to a higher call rate. New system would apply retroactively from 1 Jan 2028 once adopted and ratified.

Own Resources Decision needs unanimity in the Council after consulting the European Parliament, then ratification by every Member State; Parliament's interim report of 28 Apr 2026 (370-201-84) backs the basket approach and about EUR 60 bn a year of new own resources, with no CBAM-specific rate in the press release.
legal_basis_or_document: ECA Opinion 04/2026; Council 13922/26; EP press release 23 Apr 2026 (read via WebFetch, not saved)

rule_or_fact: Federal draft budget 2027 books CBAM receipts of EUR 377.736 million as non-tax receipts in Einzelplan 60, Kap. 6002 Tit. 132 02 (managed by BMUKN); the tax chapter is Kap. 6001 'Steuern'; Kap. 6002 shows no 2026 Soll and no 2025 Ist for this title. The Bundesrat statement rounds the figure to 400 million and notes it is the first time such receipts go to the core budget.
legal_basis_or_document: BT-Drs. 21/7300 (Einzelplan 60) pp. 27 and TOC; BR-Drs. 442/26 (B) / BT-Drs. 21/8534 item 3
status_2026_10_22: government draft; Bundestag final vote planned 27 Nov 2026

rule_or_fact: No CBAM line in KTFG section 4(1) (revenue of the Klima- und Transformationsfonds); the draft KTF Wirtschaftsplan 2027 lists no CBAM receipt.

No. It is the sale price of certificates (a non-tax receipt of the selling Member State), not a tax or customs duty on the euro value of steel, and the German draft budget does not book it under 'Steuern'.
